_comment: Confirmed via live SDL2 capture on 2026-10-08. Button indices are 0-indexed pygame/SDL indices from the X45's own numbering, not vJoy's (vJoy buttons are 1-indexed virtual outputs).

mode_switch_buttons._comment: 3-way Mode switch (M1/M2/M3). Exactly one is held down at a time. Selects which layer of the layered_buttons below is active.

aux_slider_buttons._comment: 3-position Aux slider. Combined with Mode to pick 1 of 9 layers (3 mode x 3 aux), same idea the old SST .pr0 used, but done in software with real vJoy buttons instead of console macros.

disabled_buttons._comment: Physical 18-21 ('Throttle Hat' in the official Saitek driver's naming -- the dead 'finger' hat). Confirmed dead (2026-10-08/09): nothing registers in SDL2 OR the Windows/Saitek DirectInput test panel -- almost certainly a real electrical fault inside the throttle unit, not a driver/API gap. The other half of the old 18-25 range, 22-25, turned out to be the separate, working 'Mouse Hat' -- see pov4_mouse_hat below. Leave 18-21 disabled until the throttle unit is repaired and someone re-captures which indices actually move.

axes._comment: 6 analog axes confirmed working (stick X/Y, throttle, rudder, 2 rotary knobs), but which pygame axis index (0-5) is which physical control was NOT recorded. Run 'python src/remapper.py --calibrate-axes' and move one control at a time to find out, then reorder the axis_order list below to match pygame-axis-index order (position 0 in the list = pygame axis 0, etc). Each name maps to a vJoy HID usage in remapper.py's AXIS_USAGE_BY_NAME: stick_x->X, stick_y->Y, throttle->Z, rudder->Rx, knob_1->Ry, knob_2->Rz. Plain Generic Desktop axes only (X/Y/Z/Rx/Ry/Rz) -- tried this vJoy fork's dedicated Rudder/Throttle/Slider/Dial axes but they sit on non-standard usage IDs that generic axis parsers don't recognize (confirmed via the Windows joystick test panel), so they don't actually register anywhere. The order below is a guess for first boot and likely needs reordering after calibration.

pov1._comment: Main hat switch (official driver name: 'POV 1'), the one true continuous SDL hat object. Passed straight through to vJoy continuous POV #1, same in every Mode/Aux layer.

pov2._comment: Small left-thumb mini-hat on the throttle grip (official driver name: 'POV 2'), confirmed working. SDL reports it as 4 separate digital buttons rather than a real hat, so the remapper synthesizes a POV direction from their combined state (supports diagonals if the hardware can report two adjacent directions at once) and drives vJoy continuous POV #2. Deliberately NOT layered by Mode/Aux -- same direction in every layer, matching how the Saitek driver itself treats it as a plain hat. Physical button order is clockwise from Up (14=Up,15=Right,16=Down,17=Left), NOT the up/down/left/right sequence the original button-map notes assumed -- corrected live (2026-10-09) after the vJoy POV2 output came out rotated.

pov3_throttle_hat._comment: Official driver name: 'Throttle Hat' (the 'finger' hat). Confirmed dead hardware on the original dev's unit (2026-10-08/09) -- physical 18-21, see disabled_buttons above. Left disabled by default for anyone else cloning this repo too, since there's no way to verify directions on hardware that doesn't respond. If YOUR Throttle Hat works: the buttons guess below is UNVERIFIED, extrapolated from POV2's clockwise-from-Up pattern (18=Up,19=Right,20=Down,21=Left) -- confirm it's actually right with 'python src/remapper.py --calibrate-buttons' (press one direction at a time, note which index fires) before trusting it, then flip enabled to true.

pov4_mouse_hat._comment: Official driver name: 'Mouse Hat'. Isolated live (2026-10-09) from the dead 'Throttle Hat' -- they're both inside the physical 18-25 range, but Mouse Hat is physical 22-25 and confirmed working, while 18-21 (Throttle Hat) stayed silent through the same test. Strict 4-way switch, no diagonals (confirmed: pressing between two directions only ever fired one button). Drives vJoy continuous POV #4, same in every Mode/Aux layer.
